title: Phoolon Ki Holi and Lathmar Holi: What to Wear and Why It Matters
excerpt: Phoolon ki Holi and Lathmar Holi explained simply, with what to wear for temple visits, flower showers and lively crowds in Vrindavan and Barsana.
body:
For Phoolon ki Holi and Lathmar Holi, wear a modest, comfortable cotton kurta set with a dupatta, slip-on flats you can remove at temples and minimal jewellery. These are joyful, crowded and deeply devotional celebrations, so dress for respect and movement first, style second. Here is what each tradition is, explained simply, and how to dress for it.

## The Braj region and its Holi traditions

The Braj region around Mathura, Vrindavan, Barsana and Nandgaon is linked with the stories of Radha and Krishna, and its Holi celebrations are among the most famous in India. Festivities here begin in the days before the main Holi, which in 2027 falls on 22 March, and each town has its own customs. Two of the best known are Phoolon ki Holi and Lathmar Holi.

## Phoolon ki Holi: the Holi of flowers

Phoolon ki Holi is celebrated in temples in Vrindavan. Instead of coloured powder, priests shower devotees with flower petals, and the temple fills with music, bhajans and a sea of marigold and rose. It is gentle, beautiful and spiritual, and people from around the world come to experience it.

**What to wear:** since the mood is devotional and the petals are soft, this is a good time for white or pastels. A [mint green block print kurta set with hand work yoke](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) looks fresh among the flowers and is modest and comfortable.

If you prefer white, the [off-white embroidered cotton kurta set with organza dupatta](/products/off-white-embroidered-cotton-flex-kurta-pant-organza-dupatta-set/) feels graceful for a temple visit.

## Lathmar Holi: the Holi of sticks

Lathmar Holi is famous in Barsana and Nandgaon. In the story, Krishna came from Nandgaon to tease Radha and her friends in Barsana, and they playfully chased him away with sticks. Today, men from Nandgaon visit Barsana and the women playfully strike at them with lathis, or long sticks, while the men protect themselves with shields. There is plenty of colour, singing and huge crowds, and it is all done in a spirit of fun and tradition.

**What to wear:** expect lots of colour and crowds. Choose durable cotton in a print or bright shade, avoid long trailing dupattas and wear secure footwear. The [grey block print kurta set with Kota Doria dupatta](/products/grey-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-kota-doria-dupatta-set/) is a practical choice.

A [yellow embroidered tunic with black floral yoke](/products/yellow-black-embroidered-cotton-tunic-top/) with comfortable pants also works well, and the print hides marks.

## What to wear, side by side

| | Phoolon ki Holi | Lathmar Holi |
|---|---|---|
| Where | Temples in Vrindavan | Barsana and Nandgaon |
| Mood | Gentle, devotional, flowers | Lively, colourful, very crowded |
| Best colours | White, mint, pastels | Prints and brights |
| Outfit | Kurta set with dupatta | Cotton kurta or tunic with pants |
| Dupatta | Draped over shoulders or head | Short or tied securely |
| Footwear | Slip-on flats for temples | Secure flats with grip |
| Jewellery | Simple and minimal | Leave valuables at home |

## Dressing respectfully for temples

These celebrations take place in and around active temples, so modest clothing matters.

- **Cover shoulders and knees.** A kurta set or tunic with full-length pants is ideal.
- **Carry a dupatta or stole.** It can be draped over your head inside a temple if you wish.
- **Choose slip-on footwear.** You will remove shoes before entering most temples, so easy flats save time.
- **Avoid tight or sheer outfits.** Breathable, opaque cotton is more comfortable for long hours and crowds.

## Practical tips for the crowds

- **Travel light.** A small zipped crossbody bag worn in front is safest.
- **Keep your phone in a waterproof pouch.**
- **Pack a change of clothes** for the journey back.
- **Tie your hair** in a braid or low bun.
- **Leave precious jewellery at home.** Crowds are dense and things get lost.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is Phoolon ki Holi?**
It is the Holi of flowers, celebrated in temples in Vrindavan, where devotees are showered with flower petals instead of coloured powder.

**What is Lathmar Holi?**
It is a playful tradition in Barsana and Nandgaon, inspired by Radha and Krishna, where women playfully strike at men with sticks while the men shield themselves.

**What should a woman wear to Lathmar Holi?**
A comfortable, opaque cotton kurta or tunic with full-length pants, secure flats and minimal jewellery. Keep your dupatta short or tied.

**Can I wear white to Phoolon ki Holi?**
Yes. White and pastels look lovely among the flower petals and suit the devotional mood.
